title: Renewable Energy
standard_code: Grade 8, Quarter 4: Force, Motion, and Energy
standard_text: Energy resources are renewable (solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, biomass) or non-renewable (coal, oil, natural gas); the Philippines uses geothermal, hydro and solar power; using energy wisely and sustainably. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 8, Quarter 4: Force, Motion, and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Force, Motion, and Energy): renewable and non-renewable resources, solar, wind, hydro and geothermal power, and saving energy. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: The Philippines is a leading user of geothermal energy.
body_html:
How to think about it

Non-renewable resources such as coal, oil and natural gas formed over millions of years and will run out; burning them releases carbon dioxide. Renewable resources such as sunlight, wind, flowing water, geothermal heat and biomass are replaced naturally.

The Philippines generates electricity from geothermal plants (such as in Leyte and Batangas), hydroelectric dams, wind farms (such as in Ilocos Norte) and solar farms. Each source has advantages and disadvantages; saving energy at home also helps.

Example

Is coal renewable?

Formed over millions of years

Answer: no

Example

Which energy uses heat from inside the Earth?

Volcanic areas

Answer: geothermal energy

Common mistakes

  • Thinking renewable means it has no environmental effects.
  • Thinking solar panels work only at noon.
  • Mixing up hydro (water) and geothermal (underground heat).

faq.q: Why does the Philippines have geothermal power?
faq.a: It has many volcanic areas where underground heat makes steam.

faq.q: Why is wind power not always available?
faq.a: The wind does not blow at the same speed all the time.

items.q: Why should you put on a sweater instead of turning up the heat?
c: It makes the house warmer for everyone.
items.e: Conserving energy reduces pollution.

items.q: Kenneth reads about a resource that formed from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how oil and natural gas formed.

items.q: Which is the main energy change in a battery-powered flashlight?

items.q: Which is used to turn wind into electricity or motion?

items.q: A stretched elastic band stores which form of energy?

items.q: Which energy source is not renewable?

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?
items.e: Wind is renewed by nature and does not run out. Coal, oil and gas take millions of years to form.

items.q: Which is a renewable energy source?
items.e: Wind will not run out.

items.q: People use a geothermal power station to get energy from heat inside Earth. Which is a benefit of this energy source?
c: It never affects the environment in any way.
It makes new energy from nothing.
It makes very little air pollution.
It works the same in every place on Earth.
items.e: It makes very little air pollution.

items.q: What does 'reduce, reuse, recycle' help save?

items.e: Making new products uses energy.

items.q: People use a dam with a power station to get energy from moving water. Which is a benefit of this energy source?

It makes new energy from nothing.
It makes no air pollution while working.
It works the same in every place on Earth.
items.e: It makes no air pollution while working.

items.q: Which is used to turn heat inside Earth into electricity or motion?
items.e: Energy from heat inside Earth is used with a geothermal power station.

items.q: People use a geothermal power station to get energy from heat inside Earth. Which is a problem with this energy source?
c: Burning gasoline pollutes the air, and oil spills harm ocean life.
It only works in places with hot rock near the surface.
Burning gas pollutes the air, and drilling can harm land and water.
Burning coal pollutes the air, and mining it damages land.
items.e: It only works in places with hot rock near the surface.

items.q: What energy change happens in a solar panel?
items.e: Solar cells change light into electricity.

items.q: Which is used to turn moving water into electricity or motion?

items.e: Energy from moving water is used with a dam with a power station.

items.q: What is a disadvantage of wind turbines?

items.e: Every source has pros and cons.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?

items.e: Copper and gold ores formed from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?

items.q: What is the difference between porosity and permeability?
c: porosity is how much open space a rock has; permeability is how easily water flows through it
permeability is the amount of water stored
porosity is how easily water flows
items.e: Clay is porous but not permeable.

items.q: What happens if groundwater is pumped faster than it is recharged?

items.q: Patricia's phone charger uses 100 J of energy and gives 80 J of useful energy. What is its efficiency?
A motor takes in 100 J and gives 25 J of useful energy. How much energy is wasted (mostly as heat)?
items.e: 100 − 25 = 75 J; it is not destroyed, just not useful.

How do humans use Earth's resources?
c: for warmth, shelter, food and transport
items.e: Natural resources are supplemented by agriculture and synthetic products.

items.q: Is coal a finite or a renewable resource?

items.q: What is sustainable development?

using resources as fast as possible
items.e: Chemists develop sustainable processes.

items.q: Why is it important to use finite resources carefully?
items.e: For example, crude oil and metal ores.

items.q: Fertilizer runoff makes algae grow over a pond. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Leave strips of plants along the water and use less fertilizer.
Replant trees and protect part of the forest as a park.
Build a treatment plant that cleans wastewater before it is released.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Leave strips of plants along the water and use less fertilizer.

items.q: A city's air is smoggy from car exhaust. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Build wind turbines and solar panels.
Add bus lines and bike lanes so fewer people drive.
Start a recycling and composting program.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Add bus lines and bike lanes so fewer people drive.

items.q: Why are LED bulbs better than old incandescent bulbs?
c: They are brighter only because they are hot.

items.e: Less energy is wasted as heat.

items.q: An old bulb uses 60 watts and an LED bulb that gives the same light uses 9 watts. A school replaces 5 old bulbs with LEDs. How many fewer watts are used when they are all on?
items.e: (60 − 9) × 5 = 255 watts. Using less electricity means less fuel burned at power stations.

items.q: Which of the three R's is sending old newspapers to make new paper?
